newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals higher on local shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals higher on local shortcovering.

text.p: New York precious metals reversed mid-session to move higher, drawing strength from COMEX May silver's determination not to break below the key $5.10 an ounce level, traders said.
Silver's resilience to hold this level prompted earlier shortcovering, which later spilled over into gold, pulling up the latter along with the white metals, traders said.
"The locals tripped over themselves and found they were a little oversold, and we also had a little light fund buying," John Geraghty of North American Equity Services said.
At 1219 EST COMEX June gold was up $0.80 at $351.30.
COMEX May silver was up 3.0 cents at $5.15 cents an ounce, traded $5.19 to $5.10.
Gold bullion also recovered by midday and was quoted by dealers at $348.00/50
Palladium wiped out its earlier losses, with NYMEX June contract up $1.20 at $148.00 an ounce.
Strength from the other precious metals was not enough to push the platinum market higher, but early losses were pared to just 50 cents in the NYMEX April contract, which traded at $375.00 an ounce.
